basis: jinshu:053:s0108 names 右衛督司馬雅 with 常從督許超, attached to the crown prince and addressing 孫秀. zizhitongjian:083:s0224 likewise names 衛督司馬雅、常從督許超 and their 東宮 service and restoration plot. The matching full name, guard post, associate and political purpose establish one man. The continued 孫秀 mission in s0244 and 雅 reply in s0246 fit this identification.

jinshu:053:s0047 reads 令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之; s0104 again names 小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來. zizhitongjian:083:s0178 records 令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之. Both concern the same named maid delivering materials for the Pan Yue draft to the intoxicated prince; this exact incident establishes identity.

Fresh jinshu:053:s0170 directly reads 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉; s0171 directly reads 虨字道文，永康元年正月，薨; s0172 grants 南陽王 posthumously. This source now expressly names 虨 and ties him to 道文, without reliance on English Bin. In contrast, jinshu:037:s0817 identifies 西河繆王斌，字子政，魏中郎, and s0820 says 咸寧四年薨，子隱立. Different Chinese given names, courtesy names 道文/子政, royal-family positions, titles, and explicit death-era statements establish distinct men. The chapter 053 child and his mother also appear in s0017; s0053/s0078/s0081/s0087/s0092 preserve the 道文 continuity. The earlier missing-glyph hold is resolved for this freshly sealed evidence, with no extraction certainty strengthened.

jinshu:053:s0192 cites 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園. sanguozhi:040:s0042 places 楚建 beside 申生、衛伋、禦寇 and says 當嗣立之正. Both are retrospective exempla of a wronged rightful heir, with the same specific Chu designation 楚建. Their explicit historical allusion, rather than shared romanization, supports one referent.

jinshu:053:s0200 appoints 孟珩為友, alongside 劉寔 and 楊准、馮蓀. songshu:047:s0085 gives 高祖珩，晉河南尹. 孟珩 and the Jin setting agree, but the companion appointment is not linked to 河南尹 or the ancestor relationship. No native-place or family match joins them. Identity is plausible but not established; both records remain separate, with no generational date inferred.

jinshu:053:s0200 says 楊准、馮蓀為文學, while jinshu:071:s0216 says 會解結代楊准為刺史. The identical Chinese full name and compatible official roles suggest a possible match, but the source does not connect the literary aide appointment to the inspectorship or supply matching family/native-place details. Keep separate as genuinely uncertain; neither incompatible chronology nor identity can be proved.

jinshu:053:s0031 gives 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮 ... 若一旦交構，大事去矣」, continued in s0032. zizhitongjian:083:s0153 gives 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」 Matching full name, exact office, same warning and Jia Mi/empress context identify one adviser.

jinshu:053:s0034 names 賈后母郭槐 and her attempt to marry 韓壽女 to the prince; zizhitongjian:083:s0126 names 廣城君郭槐 and s0128 repeats this marriage proposal. jinshu:031:s0574 calls her 后母廣城君 and s0575 describes rebuking 賈謐, matching Tongjian s0126–s0127. Chapter031 s0576 explicitly changes her title from 廣城 to 宜城, and s0578 records 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子, corresponding to Tongjian s0131. These full-name, maternal and highly specific incident matches establish one woman across all three records; s0556/s0579 and Tongjian s0077 remain compatible.

jinshu:053:s0169 reports 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台, in the crown-prince mourning episode. zizhitongjian:083:s0200 reports 西戎校尉司馬閻纘輿棺詣闕上書 and the argument about 漢戾太子. The same full Chinese name and particular appeal for the wronged heir connect the memorialist to the words moving the emperor. Tongjian s0197–s0198 gives 永康元年; s0204 identifies 圃之孫. English Yan Xun versus Yan Zuan does not override the Chinese evidence.

jinshu:053:s0169 identifies 閻纘 whose words moved the emperor; zizhitongjian:083:s0276 identifies 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭 and his earlier advice to retire. This identical name and connected Jin court context suggest one man, but the lament supplies neither the memorialist office 西戎校尉司馬 nor 圃之孫 lineage or explicit continuity. The distinct Tongjian local record remains separate under a possible match.

jinshu:053:s0200 appoints 馮蓀為文學. jinshu:004:s0198 names 侍中馮蓀 among those killed by 長沙王乂, with s0192 supplying 二年 context. Full Chinese name and court career are compatible, but the literary aide has no explicit career/family connection to the later Palace Attendant. A rare name or an inferred lifespan is insufficient proof; retain distinct records.
